---
<!-- theoremu-1: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p$, and $M$ a lisse $F$-gauge over $k$, with dual $M^\vee$. Then the trace map induces an equivalence
\[  
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}  {\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{{\mathbb Z}_p}({\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M^\vee(1)[2]),{\mathbb Z}_p) 
\]
of complexes of condensed ${\mathbb Z}_p$-modules.
<!-- end theoremu-1 -->
<!-- theoremu-2: body_md -->
For any lisse $F$-gauge
 $M^\circ$ over $k^\circ$, with base change $M$ to $k$, the sequence
 \begin{equation*}
 {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k^\circ,M^\circ) \rightarrow  {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M)\rightarrow  {\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{{\mathbb Z}_p}({\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k^\circ,M^{\circ,\vee}(1)[2]),{\mathbb Z}_p) \overset{+1}{\longrightarrow}
 \end{equation*}
induced by the duality pairing is a fibre sequence.
<!-- end theoremu-2 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
We define $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1)}_{C}$ to be the $p$-completion of the subring of $ \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0)}_{C}$ generated by $C$ and $p\partial$.
For each $n\geq 1$, we define $\mathcal{D}^{(-1)}_{C/p^n}$ to be $(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1)}_{C})/p^n$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
We denote by ${\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_C)$ the $\infty$-category of derived $p$-complete complexes of left $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_C$-modules, and by ${\bf D}(\mathcal{D}^{(m)}_k)$ the $\infty$-category of complexes of left $\mathcal{D}^{(m)}_k$-modules.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Following \cite{Dod22}, for any $m\geq 0$, we define the $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1)}_C$-submodule
\[
\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),i}_C := \left\{\left. P\in \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_C \,\right\vert\, p^iP\in \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1)}_C \right\}
\]
and the corresponding graded ring
\[
\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C:=\bigoplus_i \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),i}_C
\]
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
Let $c_m\in{\mathbb Z}_p^\times$ be $(p-1)!$ if $m\geq 1$, and $1$ if $m=0$. Then the left ideal $I$ of $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}$ generated by the degree $0$ global sections 
\[
fv-p,\;\partial^{\langle p^m \rangle_{(m-1)}}-c_mv\partial^{[p^m]}\in \mathcal{A}^{(m),0}(*)
\]
is a centralising ideal, and in particular a two-sided ideal.
The graded ring $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}/I$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The element $fv-p$ is in the centre of $\mathcal{A}^{(m)}$, and the element $\partial^{\langle p^m \rangle_{(m-1)}}-c_mv\partial^{[p^m]}$ commutes with $f,v$ and $\partial^{[p^m]}$, so to prove that $I$ is a centralising ideal it is enough to show that if $P\in \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1)}_C$, then $[\partial^{\langle p^m \rangle_{(m-1)}}-c_mv\partial^{[p^m]},P]\in I$.
But we can calculate
\begin{align*}
[\partial^{\langle p^m \rangle_{(m-1)}}-c_mv\partial^{[p^m]},P] 
&=  [\partial^{\langle p^m \rangle_{(m-1)}},P]-c_mv[\partial^{[p^m]},P] \\
&=pc_m[\partial^{[p^m]},P]_{(m-1)}-c_mfv[\partial^{[p^m]},P]_{(m-1)} \\
&=c_m[\partial^{[p^m]},P]_{(m-1)}(p-fv) \in I
\end{align*} 
That $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C\cong \mathcal{A}^{(m)}/I$ can be shown entirely similarly to the case $m=1$ handled in \cite[\S3.1]{Dod22}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
In \cite{Dod22} the ring $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0,1),\star}_C$ is described by the weaker relation $f\partial^p=p!\partial^{[p]}$.
One easily checks from the definition that the stronger relation $\partial^p=(p-1)!v\partial^{[p]}$ holds.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{defn: gauges}
A (condensed) gauge of level $m$ over $k$ is a derived $p$-complete complex of graded left $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C$-modules.
The $\infty$-category of such objects will be denoted ${\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)$.
A (condensed) $p$-torsion gauge of level $m$ over $k$ is a complex of graded left $\mathcal{D}^{(m-1,m),\star}_k$-modules, and the $\infty$-category of such objects will be denoted ${\bf D}(\mathcal{D}^{(m-1,m),\star}_k)$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem: cond abs}
Since $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C$ is derived $p$-complete, there is a t-exact equivalence of categories between ${\bf D}^{\rm perf}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)$ and the $\infty$-category of perfect complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C(*)$-modules.
Thus, although Definition \ref{defn: gauges} is rather naive (for example, we do not attempt to define a more sophisticated analytic ring structure on $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C$), the elementary category of gauges defined here will be good enough for our purposes.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}
\item
The most important example of a gauge of level $m$ is the unit gauge $C^\star:=C[f,v]/(fv-p)$, equipped with its natural $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C$-module structure coming from the standard left $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_C$-module structure on $C$.
This gauge can be visualised by the diagram
\[
\ldots  \overset{p}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} C \overset{p}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} C  \overset{1}{\underset{p}{\rightleftarrows}} C \overset{1}{\underset{p}{\rightleftarrows}} \ldots
\]
with central term sitting in graded degree $0$.
\item
By reducing the unit gauge modulo $p$, we get the unit $p$-torsion gauge $k^\star:=k[f,v]/(fv)$, visualised by the diagram
\[
\ldots  \overset{0}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} k \overset{0}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} k  \overset{1}{\underset{0}{\rightleftarrows}} k \overset{1}{\underset{0}{\rightleftarrows}} \ldots
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
If $M$ is a gauge, and $j\in {\mathbb Z}$, we define the Tate twist $M(j)$ by shifting the grading according to the rule
\[
M(j)^i = M^{i-j}
\]
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
The Tate twist $C^\star(1)$ can be visualised by the diagram
\[
\ldots  \overset{p}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} C \overset{p}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} C  \overset{p}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} C \overset{1}{\underset{p}{\rightleftarrows}} \ldots 
\]
with central term sitting in graded degree $0$.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
A $p$-torsion gauge of level $m$ over $k$, or a complex of left $\mathcal{D}_k^{(m-1)}$-modules, is called quasi-nilpotent if it is cohomologically $(\partial^{\langle p^m\rangle_{(m-1)}})^\infty$-torsion.
That is, each of its cohomology groups is the union of its $(\partial^{\langle p^m\rangle_{(m-1)}})^n$-torsion submodules.
A gauge of level $m$ over $k$, or an object of ${\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_C^{(m-1)})$, is called quasi-nilpotent if its (derived) mod $p$ reduction is quasi-nilpotent.
In each case, we will denote by ${\bf D}_{\rm qn}\subset {\bf D}$ the full subcategory of the relevant $\infty$-category consisting of quasi-nilpotent objects.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
A gauge of level $m$ is called lisse if the underlying complex of graded $C^\star$-modules is perfect.
We denote by ${\bf D}_{\rm lisse}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)\subset {\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)$ the full subcategory of lisse gauges.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
A gauge of level $m$ is called quasi-lisse if it is bounded, and each graded piece is perfect as a complex of $C$-modules.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemma: qn nilp}
Any lisse gauge is quasi-nilpotent.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We reduce modulo $p$ and replace $M$ by its cohomology groups, which are necessarily finitely generated as $C^\star$-modules.
Then $f\colon M^i\rightarrow M^{i+1}$ is an isomorphism for $i\gg 0$, and so the map $v\colon M^{i+1}\rightarrow M^i$ is zero for $i\gg 0$. 

If we fix $i_0$, then for $n$ large enough and $x\in M^{i_0}$ we have
\[
\left(\partial^{\langle p^m\rangle_{(m-1)}}\right)^n(x) = (c_mv\partial^{[p^m]})^n(x) =v^n(c_m\partial^{[p^m]})^n(x) \in v^{n-1}v(M^{i_0+n}) = 0
\]
and so $\left(\partial^{\langle p^m\rangle_{(m-1)}}\right)^n=0$ on $M^{i_0}$.
Since this is true for all $i_0$, we deduce that $M$ is quasi-nilpotent.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{theo: cdF 1}
Suppose $m\geq 0$. The functor $\sigma^*=\sigma^{*}\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)} \widehat{\otimes}^{\bf L}_{\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)}}(\,\cdot\,)$ is an equivalence of categories
\[
{\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_{C'}) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m+1)}_C)
\]
with quasi-inverse given by $\sigma^{\flat}\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)} \widehat{\otimes}^{\bf L}_{\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_{C}^{(m+1)}}(\,\cdot\,)$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
Again, since the modules $\sigma^{*}\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)}$ and $\sigma^{\flat}\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)}$ are of finite type, we can use the abstract tensor product of condensed modules; we do not need to worry about $p$-adic completion.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop: bimod isom}
Suppose $m\geq -1$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
\[
 \breve{\mathcal{D}}^{(m+1)}_{C}\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}\sigma^{*}\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)} \otimes_{\breve{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_{C'}} \sigma^{\flat}\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)} 
\]
of abstract $\breve{\mathcal{D}}^{(m+1)}_{C}$-bimodules.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
If $m\geq 0$, this follows from suitably completing \eqref{eqn: frob desc}.
If $m=-1$, this can be proved by working modulo $p^n$ for all $n$, where we proceed more or less exactly as in \cite[Proposition 2.5.2]{Ber00}, using Shiho's calculations of the PD envelopes of level $-1$ from \cite[\S2.1]{Shi15} as the key input.
Of course, strictly speaking Shiho's results do not apply in our setting, since $k$ is not smooth over its residue field ${\mathbb F}$.
 However, the fact that any uniformiser $t$ is a $p$-basis for $k$ means that the relevant calculations of divided power envelopes still work in our setting.

The crucial difference we encounter when running through the proof of \cite[Proposition 2.5.2]{Ber00} is that we must work throughout with the full PD envelopes $\mathcal{P}_{C/p^n,(0)}$ and $\mathcal{P}_{C'/p^n,(-1)}$, and we never pass to the quotients by the natural PD filtration.
This gives the required answer because
\[
\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C/p^n}^{(0)}:=\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C}^{(0)}/p^n \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\rm Hom}_{C/p^n}(\mathcal{P}_{C/p^n,(0)},C/p^n)
\]
and similarly at level $-1$. Note that we do \emph{not} get the analogous isomorphism
\[
 \mathcal{D}^{(0)}_{C/p^n} \cong \sigma^{*}\mathcal{D}_{C'/p^n}^{(-1)} \otimes_{\mathcal{D}^{(-1)}_{C'/p^n}} \sigma^{\flat}\mathcal{D}_{C'/p^n}^{(-1)} 
\]
for finite order differential operators, because the analogue of \cite[Lemme 2.3.4]{Ber00} does \emph{not} hold at level $-1$. This means that the isomorphism
\[
C/p^n\otimes_{C'/p^n} \mathcal{P}_{C'/p^n,(-1)} \otimes_{C'/p^n} C/p^n\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{P}_{C/p^n,(0)}
\]
does \emph{not} descend to an isomorphism of pro-objects
\[
\{ C/p^n\otimes_{C'/p^n} \mathcal{P}^r_{C'/p^n,(-1)} \otimes_{C'/p^n}C/p^n\}_r \cong \{\mathcal{P}^r_{C/p^n,(0)}\}_r \qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{theo: cdF 2}
Suppose $m\geq -1$. Then the functor
\[
\sigma^*=\sigma^{*}\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)} \widehat{\otimes}^{\bf L}_{\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)}}(\,\cdot\,)
\]
is an equivalence of categories
\[
{\bf D}_{\rm qn}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_{C'}) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf D}_{\rm qn}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m+1)}_C)
\]
with quasi-inverse given by $\sigma^{\flat}\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C'}^{(m)} \widehat{\otimes}^{\bf L}_{\breve{\mathcal{D}}_{C}^{(m+1)}}(\,\cdot\,)$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
As before, the tensor products here can be abstract or $p$-adic, derived or underived, the resulting functors are the same.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
An $F$-structure (or Frobenius structure) on a gauge $M$ of level $m$ is an equivalence
\[
\phi\colon \sigma^*\widehat{M}^{-\infty}\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{M}^{+\infty}
\] 
in ${\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_C)$.
An $F$-gauge of level $m$ is then a gauge of level $m$ equipped with an $F$-structure, and the category ${\bf D}_{F}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)$ of $F$-gauges of level $m$ is defined to be the (strong) equaliser of the diagram
\[
{\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)  
  \ext@arrow 0359 
  \arrowfill@ 
  \mathrel{ 
    \mathpalette 
  \raise3\hbox to 0pt{$\m@th.\relbar$\hss} 
  \lower3\hbox{$\m@th.\relbar$} 
86ex
  } 
 
  \mathrel{ 
    \mathpalette 
  \raise3\hbox to 0pt{$\m@th.\relbar$\hss} 
  \lower3\hbox{$\m@th.\relbar$} 
86ex
  } 
\rightrightarrows
{\sigma^*\widehat{(\,\cdot\,)}^{-\infty}}{\widehat{(\,\cdot\,)}^{+\infty}} 
 {\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_C) 
\]
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rem: F vs Finv and independence of sigma}
In \cite{Dod22}, such objects are called $F^{-1}$-gauges, but since the notion of $F$-gauges used there will not be relevant for us, we decided to use the slightly simpler terminology here.
It is also worth pointing out that our notion of $F$-gauge is marginally more general than that considered in \cite{Dod22} (at least, for graded $p$-complete objects), since we require an equivalence $\sigma^*\widehat{M}^{-\infty}\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{M}^{+\infty}$ rather than an equivalence $\sigma^*M^{-\infty}\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{M}^{+\infty}$.
In other words, we do not require $M^{-\infty}$ to be derived $p$-complete.
For all objects of interest to us, this distinction will be irrelevant.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{theo: F desc gauge}
If $m\geq 1$, then the functor \eqref{eqn: F bc gauge} is an equivalence of categories. If $m=0$, then \eqref{eqn: F bc gauge} induces an equivalence of categories
\[
{\bf D}_{(F),{\rm qn}}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf D}_{(F),{\rm qn}}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0,1),\star}_C) 
\]
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
It suffices to prove the claim for the categories of objects without Frobenius structure, and in fact it suffices to prove the analogous claim for $p$-torsion gauges, that is, complexes of graded left modules over $\mathcal{D}^{(m-1,m),\star}_k$.
Indeed, a straightforward $p$-completeness argument applied to ${\bf R}{\rm Hom}$'s then shows full faithfulness for $p$-complete gauges.
For essential surjectivity, we see that the essential image of $\sigma^*$ contains all $p$-torsion objects, hence all $p^n$-torsion objects by the already proved full faithfulness, and hence all $p$-complete objects.

We therefore wish to prove that the functor
\[
\sigma^* \colon{\bf D}(\mathcal{D}^{(m-1,m),\star}_k)\rightarrow {\bf D}(\mathcal{D}^{(m,m+1),\star}_k) 
\]
is an equivalence of categories if $m\geq 1$, and induces an equivalence of categories
\[
{\bf D}_{\rm qn}(\mathcal{D}^{(-1,0),\star}_k)\rightarrow {\bf D}_{\rm qn}(\mathcal{D}^{(0,1),\star}_k)
\]
if $m=0$. Since both functors are clearly exact, it is enough to prove the corresponding result for static objects.

By Theorems \ref{theo: cdF 1} and \ref{theo: cdF 2} we know that, on each graded piece, the functor $M^i\mapsto \sigma^*M^i$ is an equivalence (either for all objects if $m\geq 1$, or for quasi-nilpotent objects if $m=0$), so it suffices to show that the maps $\partial^{[p^{m}]}\colon M^i\rightarrow M^{i+1}$ can be uniquely recovered from $\partial^{[p^{m+1}]}\colon \sigma^*M^i\rightarrow\sigma^*M^{i+1}$. If $m\geq 1$, this can be done in the usual way \cite[Proposition 2.2.4]{Ber00}, since we have the explicit reconstruction
\[
M^i=\left\{ x\in \sigma^*M^i \,\left\vert\, \partial^{\langle j \rangle_{(m)}}x=0\;\; \forall p\nmid j \right. \right\}
\]
of each $M^i$ from $\sigma^*M^{i}$, and the map $\partial^{[p^{m}]}\colon M^i\rightarrow M^{i+1}$ is then simply the restriction of the map $\partial^{[p^{m+1}]}\colon \sigma^*M^i\rightarrow\sigma^*M^{i+1}$ to the subspace $M^i\subset \sigma^*M^i$.

If $m=0$, then we use \cite[Theorem 5.8]{GLSQ10} instead to recover each $M^i$ from $\sigma^*M^{i}$. One can then check by an explicit calculation that $\partial^{[p]}\colon \sigma^*M^{i}\rightarrow \sigma^*M^{i+1}$ restricts to a map $M^i\rightarrow M^{i+1}$, where it is given by $(1+g\theta)\partial$ for some $g\in \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1)}_C$. Since $M^{i+1}$ is quasi-nilpotent, the map $(1+g\theta)$ is invertible on $M^{i+1}$, thus $\partial\colon M^i\rightarrow M^{i+1}$ can be recovered from $\partial^{[p]}$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
For every $M\in {\bf D}(\mathcal{B}^{(m)})$, and every $p$-complete equivalence $N_1\rightarrow N_2$, the map $M\otimes_{C^\star}^{\bf L} N_1\rightarrow M\otimes_{C^\star}^{\bf L} N_2$ is a $p$-complete equivalence.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since $M\otimes_{C^\star}^{\mathbf{L}}$ commutes with cofibre sequences, we need to show that if $\widehat{N}=0$, then $\left(M\otimes_{C^\star}^{\bf L}N\right)^\wedge=0$. But vanishing of a derived $p$-complete complex can be checked on its mod $p$ reduction, so we need to show that if $N/^{\bf L}p=0$, then $(M\otimes^{\bf L}_{C^\star} N)/^{\bf L}p=0$, which is clear.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
${\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_C^{(m-1,m),\star})^\otimes$ is a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Since $p$-adic completion creates colimits in ${\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_C^{(m-1,m),\star})$, and is (by construction) symmetric monoidal, it is enough to show that ${\bf D}(\mathcal{B}^{(m)})^\otimes$ is presentably symmetric monoidal. Since the underlying category ${\bf D}(\mathcal{B}^{(m)})$ is stable and presentable, it is enough by \cite[Proposition 4.4.2.7]{Lur09} to show that for any given object $M\in {\bf D}(\mathcal{B}^{(m)})$, the functor $M\otimes_{C^\star}^{\bf L}$ commutes with cofibre sequences and direct sums, both of which are clear.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
Let $M$ be an ($F$-)gauge. We let $M^\vee={\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{C^\star}(M,C^\star)$ denote the dual of $M$.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
\label{defn: Mat dual}
We define the Matlis dual of a gauge $M$ by
\[
M^\lozenge := {\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{C^\star}(M,E^\star) \in {\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_C^{(m-1,m),\star})
\]
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a gauge of level $m$ over $k$. Then there is a natural fibre sequence
\[
M^\vee \xrightarrow{(f^\infty,v^\infty)} 
j^{(m)}_+(\widehat{M}^{+\infty,\vee})\oplus j^{(m-1)}_+(\widehat{M}^{-\infty,\vee}) \xrightarrow{(f^{\infty,\vee},-v^{\infty,\vee})}
M^\lozenge \overset{+1}{\longrightarrow}
\]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a lisse gauge of level $m$ over $k$.
Then $M^{\vee,\pm\infty} \simeq M^{\pm\infty,\vee}$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
The isomorphisms $\tau^i_{\beta,\beta'}$ are compatible with the actions of $f,v$ and $\partial^{[p^m]}$.
They therefore induce an isomorphism
\[
\tau_{\beta,\beta'}\colon \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_{\beta'}\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_{\beta}
\]
of condensed $(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_{C_1},\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_{C_2})$-bimodules.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
As usual, it suffices to prove compatibility on the underlying abstract modules. In this case, using the definition of $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),i}_{C_2}$ as a submodule of $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_{C_2}$, the proposition follows from applying \cite[Proposition 2.1.5]{Ber00} instead to $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_{C_2}$ as a module over itself, and then noting that Berthelot's isomorphism $\tau_{\beta,\beta'}$ is compatible with restriction of scalars along ${\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1)}\rightarrow \mathcal{D}^{(m)}$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
Suppose that either $m\geq 2$, or $m\geq 1$ and $p>2$. Then the $\infty$-category ${\bf D}_{(F)}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)$ of ($F$-)gauges of level $m$ is independent of the choice of $(C,\sigma)$ up to canonical equivalence.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
For any prime $p$, and any level $m\geq 0$, the $\infty$-category ${\bf D}_{(F),\rm qn}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m-1,m),\star}_C)$ of quasi-nilpotent ($F$-)gauges of level $m$ is independent of $(C,\sigma)$, up to canonical equivalence.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
Let $M\in  {\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C)$. We define the Nygaard cohomology of $M$ to be
\[ {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M):={\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C} (C^\star,M)  \in {\bf D}(W)  \]
This is the (condensed) $W$-linear complex of graded homomorphisms $C^\star\rightarrow M$.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
We similarly define the level $0$ and level $-1$ de\thinspace Rham cohomology of $M$ to be the condensed $W$-linear complexes
\begin{align*}
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR},(0)}(k,M) &:={\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0)}_C}(C,\widehat{M}^{+\infty})  \\
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR},(-1)}(k,M) &:={\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1)}_C}(C,\widehat{M}^{-\infty})  
\end{align*}
These are given by homomorphisms $C^\star\rightarrow M$ after applying the functors $\widehat{(\,\cdot\,)}^{+\infty}$ and $\widehat{(\,\cdot\,)}^{-\infty}$.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
Let $M\in  {\bf D}_F(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C)$. We define the syntomic cohomology of $M$ to be
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M):={\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{ {\bf D}_F(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C)}(C^\star,M) \in {\bf D}({\mathbb Z}_p)
\]
This is the condensed ${\mathbb Z}_p$-linear complex of homomorphisms $C^\star\rightarrow M$ in  ${\bf D}_F(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C)$.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop: cohom explicit 1}
Let $M$ be a gauge of level $0$ over $k$.
Then the Nygaard and de\thinspace Rham cohomologies of $M$ are given by the totalisations of the following double complexes
\begin{align*}
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M)&= \left[ M^0 \overset{\nabla}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C M^1\right] \\
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR},(0)}(k,M)&= \left[ \widehat{M}^{+\infty} \overset{\nabla}{\longrightarrow}  \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C \widehat{M}^{+\infty} \right] \\
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR},(-1)}(k,M)&= \left[ \widehat{M}^{-\infty} \overset{\nabla^{(-1)}}{\longrightarrow}  \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C \widehat{M}^{-\infty}\right]
\end{align*}
Here $\nabla^{(-1)}$ is the map defined by $\nabla^{(-1)}(x)={{\rm d}}t\otimes \theta(x)$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor: deRham from Nygaard}
Let $M\in {\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(m)}_C)$, for $m=-1,0$. Then
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR},(m)}(k,M)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,j^{(m)}_+M)
\]
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor: syn coh explicit}
Let $M$ be an $F$-gauge of level $0$ over $k$. Then ${\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M)$ is represented by the totalisation of the triple complex 
\[ 
\xymatrix{
 M^0 \ar[r]^-{\nabla}  \ar[d]_-{f^\infty-\phi^\flat v^\infty} &
\widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C M^1   \ar[d]^-{1\otimes f^\infty- \frac{\sigma}{p}\otimes \phi^{\flat}v^\infty} \\
 \widehat{M}^{+\infty} \ar[r]^-{\nabla} &
 \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C \widehat{M}^{+\infty}
 }
 \]
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
A virtual $F$-crystal over $k$ is a finite free $C$-module $\mathcal{M}$, together with a connection and a horizontal isomorphism
\[
\varphi\colon \sigma^*\mathcal{M}[1/p]\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{M}[1/p]
\]
The category of such objects will be denoted ${\bf vF}\text{-}{\bf Cris}_k$.
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a static gauge (of any level $m$) over $k$.
We say that $M$ is rigid if the maps
\[
f\colon M^i/v \rightarrow M^{i+1}/v,\qquad v\colon M^i/f\rightarrow M^{i-1}/f
\]
are injective, for all $i$.
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
Let $M$ be an $F$-gauge of level $1$ over $k$. Then $M$ is in the essential image of \eqref{eqn: g1} if and only if it is static, lisse, $p$-torsion free and rigid.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{theo: syn cohom complex 2}
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a virtual $F$-crystal over $k$.
Then ${\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,\mathfrak{g}^{(0)}\mathcal{M})$ is represented by the totalisation of the double complex 
\[
\xymatrix{
{\rm F}^0_\EuScript{N}\mathcal{M}\ar[r]^-\nabla \ar[d]_{1-\varphi^\flat_0} & \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C{\rm F}^{-1}_\EuScript{N}\mathcal{M} \ar[d]^{1-\frac{\sigma}{p}\otimes \varphi^\flat_{-1}} \\
\mathcal{M} \ar[r]^-{\nabla} & \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C\mathcal{M}
}
\]
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
\label{defn: DM gaugelike}
We say that a Dieudonn\'e module $M\in {\bf DM}_C$ is gauge-like if $(p-1)!F\partial^{[p]}V=\partial^p$ as maps $M\rightarrow M$. We denote the full subcategory of such objects by ${\bf DM}_C^{\mathfrak{g}}$.
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
\label{exa: non gauge-like}
Let $M=ke_1\oplus ke_2$ be free of rank $2$ over $k$, with connection given by $\nabla(e_1)={\rm d} t\otimes t^{p-1}e_2$, $\nabla(e_2)=0$.
Set $F=V=0$.
Then $M$ is a Dieudonn\'e module over $C$.
Since $F=V=0$ we see immediately that $(p-1)!F\partial^{[p]}V=0$, however, $\partial^p(e_1)=\partial^{p-1}(t^{p-1})e_2=-e_2\neq 0$. 
Hence $M$ is not gauge-like, although it is quasi-nilpotent.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lemma: psirig}
Let $G$ be either a finite flat group scheme or a $p$-divisible group over $k$. Then $\mathbb{M}(G)$ is gauge-like.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
If $G$ is a $p$-divisible group, then $\mathbb{M}(G)$ is torsion-free, and hence gauge-like.
If $H$ is a finite flat group scheme, then by \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 3.1.1]{BBM82} there exists an injective map $H\hookrightarrow G$ with $G$ a $p$-divisible group.
This induces a surjective map $\mathbb{M}(G/H)\rightarrow \mathbb{M}(H)$, where $G/H$ is $p$-divisible, and the fact that $\mathbb{M}(H)$ is gauge-like follows from the fact that $\mathbb{M}(G/H)$ is.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
We define $\mathfrak{g}^{(1)}\colon {\bf FG}_k\rightarrow {\bf D}_{F,{\rm lisse}}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0,1),\star}_C)$ and $\mathfrak{g}^{(1)}\colon {\bf BT}_k\rightarrow {\bf D}_{F,{\rm lisse}}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0,1),\star}_C)$ as the composite functors
\begin{align*}
{\bf FG}_k& \overset{\mathbb{M}}{\longrightarrow}{\bf DM}_C^{\mathfrak{g}}\longrightarrow {\bf D}_{F,{\rm lisse}}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0,1),\star}_C)  \\
 {\bf BT}_k &\overset{\mathbb{M}}{\longrightarrow}{\bf DM}_C^{\mathfrak{g}}\longrightarrow {\bf D}_{F,{\rm lisse}}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(0,1),\star}_C)
 \end{align*}
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
\label{exa: standard ffgs}
We consider the finite flat group schemes ${\mathbb Z}/p^n$, $\mu_{p^n}$ and $\alpha_p$ over $k$. Then $\mathfrak{g}^{(1)}{\mathbb Z}/p^n=C^\star/p^n$, $\mathfrak{g}^{(1)}\mu_{p^n}=C^\star(1)/p^n$, and $\mathfrak{g}^{(1)}\alpha_p$ is the $F$-gauge given by
\[
\ldots  \overset{0}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} k \overset{0}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} k  \overset{0}{\underset{0}{\rightleftarrows}} k \overset{1}{\underset{0}{\rightleftarrows}} \ldots 
\]
where the central term sits in graded degree $0$.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
Suppose that $p>2$, and let $G$ be a $p$-divisible group over $k$. Then there is a natural equivalence
\[
{\bf R}\underset{n}{\mathrm{lim}}\,{\bf R}\Gamma(k,G[p^n]) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,\mathfrak{g}^{(0)}G)(*)
\]
of complexes of abstract ${\mathbb Z}_p$-modules.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor: syn coh flat}
Suppose that $p>2$, and let $H$ be a finite flat group scheme over $k$ of $p$-power order. Then there is a natural equivalence
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma(k,H) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,\mathfrak{g}^{(0)}H)(*)
\]
of complexes of abstract ${\mathbb Z}_p$-modules.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
We define the trace map ${\mathrm{Tr}}\colon \Omega^1_k\rightarrow {\mathbb F}_p$ as the composite of ${\mathrm{Res}}$ with the usual Galois-theoretic trace map ${\mathrm{Tr}}_{{\mathbb F}/{\mathbb F}_p}\colon {\mathbb F}\rightarrow {\mathbb F}_p$.
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop: pd k} Let $N$ be a perfect complex of $k$-modules, with $k$-linear dual complex $N^\vee:={\bf R}{\rm Hom}_k(N,k)$. Then the map \[ \left(\Omega^1_k\otimes_k N^\vee \right)\otimes^{\bf L}_k N  \overset{\rm ev}{\longrightarrow} \Omega^1_k \overset{\mathrm{Tr}}{\longrightarrow} {\mathbb F}_p \]
 induces an equivalence
 \[ \Omega^1_k  \otimes_k N^\vee  \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{{\mathbb F}_p}(N,{\mathbb F}_p) \]
in ${{\bf D}}({\mathbb F}_p)$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
We immediately reduce to the case $N=k$ and ${\mathbb F}={\mathbb F}_p$. Choosing a uniformiser $t$, the given pairing can be identified with the map
\begin{align*}
{\mathbb F}_p(\!(t)\!) \times {\mathbb F}_p(\!(t)\!) &\rightarrow {\mathbb F}_p \\
\left(\sum_i a_it^i ,\sum_i b_it^i\right)&\mapsto \sum_i a_ib_{-i}
\end{align*}
We therefore reduce to showing that the pairing
\begin{align*}
\bigoplus_{\mathbb N} {\mathbb F}_p  \times \prod_{\mathbb N} {\mathbb F}_p &\rightarrow {\mathbb F}_p \\
\left(a_i, b_i \right)&\mapsto \sum_i a_ib_i
\end{align*}
induces equivalences
\begin{align*}
\prod_{{\mathbb N}} {\mathbb F}_p &\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{{\mathbb F}_p}(\bigoplus_{\mathbb N} {\mathbb F}_p,{\mathbb F}_p)\\
\bigoplus_{{\mathbb N}} {\mathbb F}_p &\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{{\mathbb F}_p}(\prod_{\mathbb N} {\mathbb F}_p,{\mathbb F}_p)
\end{align*}
The first of these follows more or less immediately from the definitions, using the fact that countable products of (light) condensed abelian groups are exact. 

For the second, it follows from \cite[proof of Theorem 3.2.4(9)]{RC26} that the right hand side is concentrated in degree $0$, and a straightforward calculation shows that the given map is an isomorphism in this degree.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lemma: check dense}
Let $\psi,\xi\colon C\rightarrow W$ be homomorphisms of condensed $W$-modules, and let $t\in C(*)$ be a uniformiser lift.
If $\psi(t^i)=\xi(t^i)$ for all $i\in {\mathbb Z}$, then $\psi=\xi$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Since $W$ is $p$-adically complete, it is enough to show that $\psi=\xi$ as maps $C/p^n\rightarrow W/p^n$, for all $n$.
Next, writing $C/p^n = \underset{m}{\mathrm{colim}}\, t^{-m} W/p^n\llbracket t \rrbracket$ it is enough to show that $\psi=\xi$ as maps $t^{-m} W/p^n\llbracket t \rrbracket\rightarrow W/p^n$, for all $m$ and $n$.
But now $t^{-m} W/p^n\llbracket t \rrbracket$ and $W/p^n$ are both light profinite sets, and so it suffices to observe that $W/p^n$ is Hausdorff and that $t^{-m} W/p^n[t] \subset t^{-m} W/p^n\llbracket t \rrbracket$ is dense.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
The map $\mathrm{Res}$ is independent of $t$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{lemma: check dense} it is enough to show that if $s\in C(*)$ is another such choice of uniformiser lift, then
\[
\mathrm{Res}(s^i{\rm d}\!\log s)=\begin{cases} 1& i=0 \\ 0& i\neq 0\end{cases}
\]
If $i\neq 0$ then this is easy: we simply calculate  
\[
is^i\,{\rm d}\!\log s={\rm d} s^i = t\partial(s^i)\,{\rm d}\!\log t
\]
and then observe that $t\partial(s^i)$ clearly has no constant term, and that $W$ is torsion-free.

If $i=0$, we write $s=tu_0u_1$ where $u_0\in W\llbracket t \rrbracket^\times$ and $u_1\in 1+pC$.
Then 
\[
\log u_1 = -\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{(1-u_1)^n}{n}
\]
converges in $C$, and so we find that
\[
{\rm d}\!\log s = {\rm d}\!\log t + tu_0^{-1}\partial u_0\cdot {\rm d}\!\log t + {\rm d}( \log u_1)
\]
and the second and third terms visibly have zero residue in $t$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
The map $\mathrm{Tr}_{W/{\mathbb Z}_p}\circ \mathrm{Res}\colon \widehat{\Omega}^{1}_C\rightarrow {\mathbb Z}_p $ vanishes on the images of both ${\rm d}\colon C\rightarrow\widehat{\Omega}^{1}_C$ and $1-\frac{\sigma}{p}\colon  \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\rightarrow \widehat{\Omega}^{1}_C$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
That $\mathrm{Tr}_{W/{\mathbb Z}_p}\circ \mathrm{Res}\circ {\rm d}=0$ is immediate, since we already have $\mathrm{Res}\circ {\rm d}=0$ by inspection.
We next show that ${\rm Res}$ intertwines $\frac{\sigma}{p}$ with the usual Witt vector Frobenius $\sigma$ on $W$. Indeed, by Lemma \ref{lemma: check dense}, it is enough to show that ${\rm Res}(\frac{\sigma}{p}(t^i\,{\rm d}\!\log t))=0$ for $i\neq 0$, and that ${\rm Res}(\frac{\sigma}{p}({\rm d}\!\log t))=1$. For the former, we calculate  
\[
i\sigma(t^i\,{\rm d}\!\log t) = \sigma ({\rm d} t^i) = {\rm d}\sigma(t^i)
\]
which shows that $ip\cdot {\rm Res}(\frac{\sigma}{p}(t^i\,{\rm d}\!\log t))=0$. Thus ${\rm Res}(\frac{\sigma}{p}(t^i\,{\rm d}\!\log t))=0$ since $W$ is torsion-free. For the latter, we write $\sigma(t)=t^pu$ for some $u\in 1+pC$. As before,
\[ \frac{\log u}{p} = -\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{p^{n-1}\left(\frac{1-u}{p}\right)^n}{n} \]
converges in $C$, and so
\[ \frac{\sigma}{p}({\rm d}\!\log t)=  {\rm d}\!\log t +{\rm d}(\frac{\log u}{p})\]
which clearly has residue $1$. To complete the proof, we now observe that, for any $\omega\in \widehat{\Omega}^1_C$,
\[ {\rm Res}((1-\tfrac{\sigma}{p})\omega) = (1-\sigma){\rm Res}(\omega) \]
and ${\rm Tr}_{W/{\mathbb Z}_p}$ vanishes on the image of $1-\sigma$ by Galois theory for $W/{\mathbb Z}_p$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
We define the trace map
\[ \mathrm{Tr}\colon {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,C^\star(1)[2]) \rightarrow {\mathbb Z}_p \]
to be the composite
\[ {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,C^\star(1)[2])\longrightarrow {\rm H}^2_{\rm Syn}(k,C^\star(1)) \xrightarrow{ \mathrm{Tr}_{W/{\mathbb Z}_p}\circ \mathrm{Res}} {\mathbb Z}_p \]
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop: pd C}
Let $M$ be a perfect complex of $C$-modules. Then the map
\[ \left( \widehat{\Omega}^1_C \otimes_C M^\vee\right) \otimes_C^{\bf L} M\overset{\rm ev}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{\Omega}^1_C \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Tr}_{W/{\mathbb Z}_p}\circ \mathrm{Res}} {\mathbb Z}_p  \]
induces an equivalence
\[ \widehat{\Omega}^1_C \otimes_C M^\vee \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{{\mathbb Z}_p}(M,{\mathbb Z}_p) \]
in ${{\bf D}}({\mathbb Z}_p)$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
This reduces via a $p$-completeness argument to Proposition \ref{prop: pd k}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
Let $M\in {\bf D}(\widehat{\mathcal{D}}_C^{(-1,0),\star})$ be a quasi-lisse gauge over $k$. 
Then the double duality map
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M)\rightarrow {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M)^{**}
\]
is an equivalence.
If $M^{\pm\infty}$ is a perfect complex of $C$-modules, then the same is true for de\thinspace Rham cohomology, and if $M$ is a lisse $F$-gauge, then the same is true for syntomic cohomology.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Since de\thinspace Rham cohomology is a special case of Nygaard cohomology, by Corollary \ref{cor: deRham from Nygaard}, and syntomic cohomology sits in a fibre sequence with Nygaard and de\thinspace Rham cohomology, it suffices to treat the case of Nygaard cohomology.
We can then use Proposition \ref{prop: cohom explicit 1} to compute the Nygaard cohomology of $M$ as the double complex
\[
M^0 \overset{\nabla}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C M^1
\]
We now simply note that $M^0$ and $M^1$ are perfect complexes over $C$, and hence reflexive by Proposition \ref{prop: pd C}.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop: star-diamond}
Let $M$ be a quasi-lisse gauge over $k$.
Then the map \eqref{eqn: Mat linear} is $\widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C$-linear.
In particular, there is a natural equivalence
\[
M^\lozenge \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} M^* \otimes_C \widehat{\Omega}^{1,\vee}_C
\]
of quasi-lisse gauges.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
We need to show that for any $P\in \widehat{\mathcal{D}}^{(-1,0),\star}_C$, the map
\[
\xymatrix{
\widehat{\Omega}^1_C \otimes_C M^\lozenge \ar[d]_{\cdot P}\ar[r] & M^* \ar[d]^{(P\cdot )^*} \\
\widehat{\Omega}^1_C \otimes_C M^\lozenge \ar[r] & M^* 
}
\]
commutes, for which it is sufficient to show that 
\[
{\rm Res}(\omega(Px)) = {\rm Res}((\omega P)x)
\]
for any $\omega \in \widehat{\Omega}^1_C  \otimes_C M^\lozenge$, $x\in M$. We already know $C$-linearity, so it suffices to treat the three cases $P=f,v,\partial$.
The first two are straightforward. 

For the last, if we have $\omega\in \widehat{\Omega}^1_C \otimes_C M^{\lozenge,i}=\widehat{\Omega}^1_C \otimes_C M^{-i,\vee}$, and $x\in M^{-(i+1)}$, then the Leibniz rule for right $\mathcal{D}$-modules gives
\[
(\omega(fx))\partial =  (\omega\partial)x- \omega(\partial x)  
\]
and so 
\[
{\rm Res}((\omega\partial)x) - {\rm Res}( \omega(\partial x)) = {\rm Res}((\omega(fx))\partial) =0
\]
as required.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{theo: main1} Let $M$ be a lisse $F$-gauge over $k$.
Then the evaluation pairing
\[
M\widehat{\otimes}^{\bf L}_{C^\star} M^\vee(1) \rightarrow C^\star(1)
\]
composed with the trace map 
\[
\mathrm{Tr}\colon {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,C^\star(1)[2]) \rightarrow {\mathbb Z}_p
\]
induces an equivalence
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M)  \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M^\vee(1)[2])^*
\]
in ${\bf D}({\mathbb Z}_p)$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop: N dual} Let $M$ be a quasi-lisse gauge over $k$. Then the pairing
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M)\widehat{\otimes}^{\bf L}_{{\mathbb Z}_p}{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M^\lozenge(1)[1]) \overset{{\rm ev}}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,E^\star(1)[1]) \overset{\rm Tr}{\longrightarrow} {\mathbb Z}_p 
\]
induces an equivalence
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M^\lozenge(1)[1])^*
\]
in ${\bf D}({\mathbb Z}_p)$.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
We may assume that $M$ is static, in which case each graded piece is a finitely generated $C$-module. 
Note that by Propositions \ref{prop: cohom explicit 1} and \ref{prop: star-diamond}, the ${\mathbb Z}_p$-linear dual of 
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M) = \left[ M^0 \overset{\nabla}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C M^1 \right]
\]
is computed by the totalisation of the complex
\[
\left[ M^{\lozenge,-1} \overset{\nabla}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{\Omega}^1_C\otimes_C M^{\lozenge,0} \right]
\]
with $M^{\lozenge,-1}$ sitting in horizontal cohomological degree $-1$, and the implicit pairing being given by the trace map.
Again, by Proposition \ref{prop: cohom explicit 1}, we therefore see that the trace map induces an equivalence
\[ 
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M)^*\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}  {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M^\lozenge(1)[1])
\]
and so replacing $M$ by $M^\lozenge(1)[1]$ and using $(M^\lozenge)^\lozenge=M$ gives the result.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
A(n $F$-)gauge over $k^\circ$ is said to be lisse if it is perfect as a complex of graded $C^{\circ,\star}$-modules.
It is said to be quasi-lisse if it is bounded, and each graded piece is a perfect complex over $C^\circ$.
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem: tors gauge}
We note that a lisse $F$-gauge over $k^\circ$ can have both $p$-torsion and $t$-torsion. For example, we can consider the gauge
\[
\ldots  \overset{0}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} k^\circ/(t) \overset{0}{\underset{1}{\rightleftarrows}} k^\circ/(t)  \overset{0}{\underset{0}{\rightleftarrows}} k^\circ/(t^{p}) \overset{1}{\underset{0}{\rightleftarrows}} \ldots
\]
with central term sitting in graded degree $0$, where each term has its canonical $\mathcal{D}^{(-1)}_{k^\circ}$-module structure, and where $\partial$ acts trivially in non-positive degrees, and in the canonical way in positive degrees.
The Frobenius structure is the canonical isomorphism $\sigma^*(k^\circ/(t)) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} k^\circ/(t^{p})$.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{theo: lagrange}
The square \eqref{eqn: fibre square} is a fibre square.
That is, for any lisse $F$-gauge
 $M^\circ$ over $k^\circ$, with base change $M$ to $k$, the sequence
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn: fibre}
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k^\circ,M^\circ) \longrightarrow
 {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k,M)\longrightarrow
  {\bf R}\Gamma_{\rm Syn}(k^\circ,M^{\circ,\vee}(1)[2])^* \overset{+1}{\longrightarrow}
  \end{equation}
 is a fibre sequence.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lemma: pont dual orthog}
Let $M^\circ$ be a perfect complex of $C^\circ$-modules, with $C^\circ$-linear dual complex $M^{\circ,\vee}:={\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{C^\circ}(M^\circ,C^\circ)$, and base change $M:=M^\circ\otimes^{\bf L}_{C^\circ}C$ to $C$.
Then the equivalence
\[
 M\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} \left(\widehat{\Omega}^1_{C} \otimes_C M^\vee\right)^*
\]
from Proposition \ref{prop: pd C} induces a fibre sequence
\[
M^\circ \longrightarrow M \longrightarrow \left(\widehat{\Omega}^1_{C^\circ} \otimes_{C^\circ}  M^{\circ,\vee}\right)^*\overset{+1}{\longrightarrow}
\]
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
We may replace $M^\circ$ first by its reduction modulo $p$, and then by its cohomology groups. 
It is then straightforward to reduce to the case ${\mathbb F}={\mathbb F}_p$, and we can treat separately the case where $M^\circ$ is a finite free $k^\circ\cong {\mathbb F}_p\llbracket t \rrbracket$-module, and where $M^\circ$ is $t^\infty$-torsion. We can reduce the former to the case $M^\circ={\mathbb F}_p\llbracket t \rrbracket$, and the latter to the case $M^\circ=k^\circ/(t)={\mathbb F}_p$. 

If $M^\circ=k^\circ$, then the essential claim is that, under the duality pairing
\[
{\mathbb F}_p(\!(t)\!) \times {\mathbb F}_p(\!(t)\!)\, {\rm d}\!\log t \rightarrow {\mathbb F}_p,\qquad (\alpha,\beta\,{\rm d}\!\log t)\mapsto {\rm Res}(\alpha\beta \,{\rm d}\!\log t)
\]
the orthogonal complement of ${\mathbb F}_p\llbracket t \rrbracket\subset {\mathbb F}_p(\!(t)\!)$ is ${\mathbb F}_p\llbracket t \rrbracket\, {{\rm d} t}\subset {\mathbb F}_p(\!(t)\!)\, {\rm d}\!\log t$, which is a routine calculation. If $M^\circ={\mathbb F}_p$, then the claim is that 
\[
{\bf R}{\rm Hom}_{{\mathbb F}_p\llbracket t \rrbracket}({\mathbb F}_p,\Omega^1_{{\mathbb F}_p\llbracket t \rrbracket}) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\mathbb F}_p[-1]
\]
which is, again, a routine calculation.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop: N lagrange}
Let $M^\circ$ be a quasi-lisse gauge over $k^\circ$, with base change $M$ to $k$.
Then the equivalence
\[
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M) \overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow} {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M^\lozenge(1)[1])^*
\]
of Proposition \ref{prop: N dual} induces a fibre sequence
 \begin{equation*}
 {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k^\circ,M^\circ) \longrightarrow  
 {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M)\longrightarrow 
 {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k^\circ,M^{\circ,\lozenge}(1)[1])^* \overset{+1}{\longrightarrow}
 \end{equation*}
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
We immediately reduce to the case where $M^\circ$ is static. Then
\begin{align*}
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k^\circ,M^\circ) &= {\rm fib}\left[M^{\circ,0} \overset{\nabla}{\longrightarrow}
\widehat{\Omega}^1_{C^\circ} \otimes_{C^\circ} M^{\circ,1} \right] \\
{\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M) &= {\rm fib}\left[M^{0} \overset{\nabla}{\longrightarrow}
\widehat{\Omega}^1_{C} \otimes_{C} M^1 \right]
\end{align*}
and so by Lemma \ref{lemma: pont dual orthog} the cofibre of ${\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k^\circ,M^\circ)\rightarrow {\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k,M)$ is given by the totalisation of the complex
\[
\left(\widehat{\Omega}^1_{C^\circ} \otimes_{C^\circ}  M^{\circ,0,\vee}\right)^* \longrightarrow \left(  M^{\circ,1,\vee}\right)^*
\]
with terms sitting in horizontal cohomological degrees $0$ and $1$. But we can identify this with
\[
 \left( M^{\circ,\lozenge,-1} \longrightarrow  \widehat{\Omega}^1_{C^\circ} \otimes_{C^\circ}  M^{\circ,\lozenge,0}\right)^*
\]
where the complex inside the brackets sits in horizontal cohomological degrees $-1$ and $0$, and is hence nothing other than ${\bf R}\Gamma_{\EuScript{N}}(k^\circ,M^{\circ,\lozenge}(1)[1])$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
If $p>2$, then \cite[Theorem 1.1]{TV24} also applies over $k^\circ$. Hence the fact that the analogue of Theorem \ref{theo: syn cohom complex 2} holds over $k^\circ$ means that the analogue of Corollary \ref{cor: syn coh flat} also holds over $k^\circ$. In particular, we can recover the classical orthogonality results for flat cohomology (that is, \cite[Corollary III.7.2]{Mil86}) from Theorem \ref{theo: lagrange}, at least once we know injectivity of the map
\begin{equation} \label{eqn: int flat coh} {\rm H}^*_{\rm Syn}(k^\circ,\mathfrak{g}^{(0)}H)\rightarrow {\rm H}^*_{\rm Syn}(k,\mathfrak{g}^{(0)}H)\end{equation}
whenever $H$ is a finite flat group scheme (of $p$-power order) over $k^\circ$. But, given the equivalence with flat cohomology, the argument that \eqref{eqn: int flat coh} is an isomorphism in degree $0$ and injective in degree $1$ is completely elementary, and this is then enough to show vanishing of the left hand side of \eqref{eqn: int flat coh} in all higher degrees by self-duality of the fibre sequence \eqref{eqn: fibre}. Thus we obtain the required injectivity.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
